- A PREMISE LIST THE SYSTEM CANNOT READ IS REPORTED, NEVER FORFEITED (ASK 626; nodes `D3 Build`, `C3 Build`, `C3 Extract`, `D4 Build`, `C4 Build`, `C2B Extract`, `D3B Extract`, `C3B Extract`, `Assume Check Build`, `Build Save Body`, `Format Markdown`, `Panel Build`, `Build Independent Verdict` and the Shared Library; the child holds no list reader and is unchanged; no model setting and no instruction to a judge or a debater is changed):
  - What it does, the head form: every reader of an UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES list takes one head form: optional heading marks ("#" to "######"), optional bold marks, the number, "." or ")", optional closing bold marks, then a space. So "1.", "1)", "**1.**", "### 1." and "#### **1.**" each begin a premise; a reader that takes "LINK k:" still takes it. A "### 1." item no longer ends a list body.
  - THE STYLE LOCK: the first premise head sets the form of the list. Under a "#" heading head, a plain numbered line stays inside its premise. Under a plain head, a "#" numbered line stays inside the item it falls in. The premise count counts only heads of the first head's form.
  - LIST NOT READ: a list is not read when its heading is present with text under it, the reader finds zero premises, and the text holds no "PREMISE COUNT: 0", "none" or "no premises" line. review_notes and the transcript then print `LIST NOT READ: <side> -- the heading is present but the system read no premise under it; grade the list from the round text` in place of LINK ROUND FORFEITED. The judges' PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER prints the same line under the side's label in place of an empty side; it is the one new text a judge sees. LINK ROUND FORFEITED stays for a missing heading, "PREMISE COUNT: 0" or an empty list. The judges' own FORFEIT rule (STANDINGS, above) is unchanged: its condition, an empty list, is not met when the line says a list is present.
  - Nothing is raised or counted from a list that is not read: `pwList` returns "no list" for that side, so K-G10, K-P, K-R, the broken-press check, gate PL and the unproven-only check raise no item on it, and no count comes from it.
  - Why: a list numbered "**1.**" read as zero premises. The record then called the round forfeited, the judges received an empty ledger side, and K-G10 items went to a judge against premises whose PRESSED WITH lines stood in the round text. A reader's failure is not a debater's forfeit.
  - Shown offline: 234 checks pass on the stored rounds. Of 761 stored lists, 758 read the same count and 3 change as intended: two "**k.**" lists read 0 before and 6 now (runs 42373 and 42505), and one "### k." list with "1. 2. 3." lines inside its first premise read 3 before and 6 now (run 42234). On run 42373 the K-G10 items against the challenger go from 2 to 0 and no FORFEITED line is printed. `Assume Check Build` now reads two older lists written "### k. LINK Dk" (0 before; 6 and 1 now). No stored run would print LIST NOT READ.
  - Limits: node code is not served the Library, so each node holds its own copy of the head form; the offline test runs every copy and fails on one that reads differently. The readers with no body-end stop (`C3 Extract`, `C3 Build`, `C4 Build`, and the Library's unanswered-press reader and OAN harvest) take "#" section headings as premises when the first numbered line after the heading is a "#" section heading; on the one stored round of that form their items go from 6 to 7 with equal output, because that text holds no PRESSED WITH line.
  - Not shown by a run: no live run has gone through a bold or heading-numbered list, and none has printed LIST NOT READ. The judges' whole ledger block was not run offline (its parts were); the first live run with such a list shows it.
